entities.summary: Arshak Jamalyan was a prominent Armenian politician who played a key role in the Armenian-Azeri conflicts of the early 20th century. As a leading figure in the Dashnak movement, Jamalyan was instrumental in shaping the country's political landscape during the First Republic of Armenia. He served as Minister of Communications to Tiflis and later as Minister of Communication of the First Republic of Armenia in 1920. Jamalyan's legacy is marked by his contributions to Armenian national identity and his efforts to promote unity among Armenians in the face of regional tensions. His impact can still be felt in modern-day Armenia, where he remains a celebrated figure in the country's political and cultural history.
